# Class 10 {.ct}

![](../graphics/REB_Logo.png){fig-alt="Reaction Engineering Basics Logo" fig-align="center" width="200"}

## Selectivity in Steady-State CSTRs {.cc}

Class 10 examines selectivity and heat transfer in steady-state CSTRs. It also illustrates a numerical procedure for completing optimization tasks.

## Learning Outcomes {.ch}

After completing Class 10 you should...

* Know the definitions and defining equations for instantaneous yield and instantaneous selectivity
* Understand
    * that typically the selectivity of parallel reactions is more strongly affected by temperature and composition than by reaction time
    * that typically the selectivity of series reactions is more strongly affected by reaction time than by temperature and composition
* Be able to
    * use instantaneous selectivity to assess how temperature and composition affect overall selectivity in reaction networks
    * use the REB assignment workflow to complete reaction engineering assignments involving optimization tasks
